body_html:
Switching school meal caterers in Dubai works best when the handover is planned a term ahead. The plan that matters covers records, dietary lists, delivery changes and how parents hear about it — not just the new menu. Treat the change as an operational project with dates and owners, and keep the switch week free of surprises.

For school, nursery and canteen meal service, see institutional catering in Dubai. This guide covers the transition between caterers.

A transition plan in four stages

StageWhat to prepareWho owns it
Before the decisionAttendance patterns, the dietary register, and a short list of current service problemsSchool administration
AnnouncementWritten notice dates, the new caterer's sample menus and a parent Q&AAdministration with the caterer
Final two weeksKitchen and storage handover, delivery schedule, access approvalsBoth caterers with the school
First weekDietary checks class by class, a service-timing trial and a feedback routeNew caterer with the school

Keep the stage table in one working document with dates. Verbal agreements between three parties rarely survive a busy term.

Records and lists to request

  • The dietary and allergen register, handled according to your own school's data practices.
  • Current menus, portion notes and any dishes classes particularly rely on.
  • Equipment, storage and refrigeration inventory — what stays, what goes.
  • Delivery access rules: gates, timings, loading points.
  • Unresolved issues and pending credits, so nothing is discovered later.

What the new caterer needs before the first delivery

  • A site visit covering kitchen, storage, serving area and delivery route.
  • The dietary list matched to classes or year groups, not just a school total.
  • Delivery windows built around break times, not around its own route.
  • The agreed approach to labelling dietary dishes.
  • One named contact at the school and one at the caterer.

Communicating the change

Send one notice, not a stream of updates: the date of change, what stays the same (meal times, the packed-lunch option, how dietary requests are submitted), and one contact for questions. Confirm every statement with the new caterer before it goes out — a promise about menus or timing that the caterer has not accepted creates the exact confusion the plan is meant to prevent.

A worked first week

Hypothetically: Monday runs a reduced menu to test delivery timing and dietary labelling; Tuesday and Wednesday run the full service with a class-by-class dietary check at the pass; Thursday collects feedback from supervisors; Friday holds a short review with the caterer and agrees corrections for week two. The point of the sequence is that every problem found early is a small fix, not a week of upset parents.

FAQ

How much notice does a caterer switch need?

Check your own agreement with the outgoing caterer for the notice and exit terms; this guide does not interpret contracts.

Can the switch happen mid-term?

It can, but the transition stages matter more: records, access handover and parent communication all need the same preparation, compressed into less time.

How should dietary registers be handed over?

Follow your school's own data practices and share only what the new caterer needs for service. Confirm the receiving process in writing before the change date.

What if the new service slips in the first week?

Agree a fallback before the switch, not after it. The What backup plan should a school ask its caterer for? lists what to have in writing before signing.

The switch succeeds when three things are written and dated: what transfers, who owns each transition stage, and how parents are told.
